title: Sing to the Lord Aloud
description: Sing to the Lord Aloud in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 81, headed “The warnings of God to his people; or, Spiritual blessings and punishments”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sing to the Lord a-loud, And make a joy-ful noise; God is our strength, our Sa-viour God; Let Is-rael hear his voice.

lines: God is our strength, our Saviour God;
"I am the Lord who set thee free
"But if ye will refuse your God,
"And let them run the dangerous road,
"Soon I would ease their sore complaints,
"And they should taste the stream that flows

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
